'''Kathleen Anne Kron''' (born 1956)<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Craven|first=L.A.|date=2011-04-29|title=Diplarche and Menziesia transferred to Rhododendron ( Ericaceae )|url=https://www.ingentaconnect.com/content/10.3767/000651911X568594|journal=Blumea - Biodiversity, Evolution and Biogeography of Plants|language=en|volume=56|issue=1|pages=34|doi=10.3767/000651911X568594|issn=0006-5196|url-access=subscription|doi-access=free}}</ref> is a retired biology professor from [[Wake Forest University]]. She is known for her research on ''[[Ericaceae]]'', a family of flowering plants.

== Education ==
Kron received her bachelor's degree  and her master's degree from [[Michigan State University]] in 1979 and 1982 respectively.<ref name="wfu">{{cite web|title=Kathleen Kron|url=http://college.wfu.edu/biology/people/faculty/kron/|url-status=dead|website=WFU Biology|accessdate=2016-03-13|archive-date=March 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160313123337/http://college.wfu.edu/biology/people/faculty/kron/}}</ref> She received her doctorate from the [[University of Florida]] in 1987.<ref name="wfu"/> In 2020, she retired as full professor from Wake Forest University.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-07-13|title=Undergraduate College {{!}} Teacher-Scholar Legacies: Kathleen Kron|url=https://college.wfu.edu/college-news/teacher-scholar-legacies/kathleen-kron/|access-date=2021-10-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210713000159/https://college.wfu.edu/college-news/teacher-scholar-legacies/kathleen-kron/|archive-date=July 13, 2021}}</ref>

Kron ran a lab concerned with the large-scale relationships between flowering plants using ''Ericaceae'' as a model organism.<ref name="wfu2">{{cite web|url=http://users.wfu.edu/kronka/kakbek/|title=Ericaceae Homepage|website=Wake Forest University|accessdate=2016-03-13}}</ref> In 2011, ''Rhododendron kroniae'' Craven, was named in honor of Kron and her work defining the evolutionary relationships within ''Ericaceae.''<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Craven|first=L.A.|date=2011-04-29|title=Diplarche and Menziesia transferred to Rhododendron ( Ericaceae )|url=https://www.ingentaconnect.com/content/10.3767/000651911X568594|journal=Blumea - Biodiversity, Evolution and Biogeography of Plants|language=en|volume=56|issue=1|pages=33–35|doi=10.3767/000651911X568594|issn=0006-5196|url-access=subscription|doi-access=free}}</ref> ''Rhododendron groenlandicum'' (Oeder) Kron & Judd is named after [[Georg Christian Oeder]], whose work was amended by Kron and [[Walter Stephen Judd]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Labrador Tea, Ledum groenlandicum, Rhododendron groenlandicum|url=https://www.friendsofthewildflowergarden.org/pages/plants/labradortea.html|access-date=2021-10-26|website=www.friendsofthewildflowergarden.org}}</ref>

The standard [[List of botanists by author abbreviation (A)|author abbreviation]] '''Kron''' is used to indicate this person as the author when [[Author citation (botany)|citing]] a [[botanical name]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kron, Kathleen Anne {{!}} International Plant Names Index|url=https://www.ipni.org/a/36400-1|access-date=2021-10-26|website=www.ipni.org}}</ref>
